fieldValues.title: Resume section/subsection purge per rfc-decision-1e7c0c8e blocked by tool gap
fieldValues.summary: Attempted the owner-ruled retirement purge for the 7 section records with a clean derived-from-only successor (Extensions, Distribution Group (Core), Conversation Layer, Foundation Group (Core), Extension Interactions, Purpose and Scope, Conformance): set meta.derivedFrom on each successor concept, then record delete the retired section record. Blocked at Work stage: srs record update silently drops a top-level meta object with no error or diagnostic on the pinned CLI (v0.1.0-build.365), so provenance was never actually captured before delete's cascade removed the derived-from relation. Reverted before committing; nothing pushed.
fieldValues.body:
## Ground

Re-measured on a fresh, unshallowed worktree off `origin/master` (e4d3ff3, which carries PR #733/rfc-decision-1e7c0c8e): `record list --type com.semanticops.spec/section` still returns all 10 original records; `/subsection` returns 61. Of the 10 sections, 7 have exactly one relation each (an inbound `derived-from` from an already-created `concept` successor, no `contains` edges remaining) and were the clean, ready-to-purge subset per the latest dispatch (comment 5620160722). Namespace Format and Schema Notation (#691's targets) still carry outbound `contains` edges to un-reparented subsection children, and Key Invariants has no successor at all (deliberately deferred, carried-context-31ea3659) — none of those three are touched by this attempt.

## What was tried

For each of the 7 clean pairs: fetched the successor's full record via `record get`, resubmitted it via `record update` with the same `fieldValues` plus `"meta": {"derivedFrom": "<original-instanceId>"}`, then `record delete`d the original (the pinned build has no `--cascade` flag — srs-rust#1028 has not reached this repo's pin, `SRS_RUST_CLI_TAG` in `.github/workflows/release-drift.yml` is still `v0.1.0-build.365` — so this fell back to the pre-#1028 silent-cascade delete the ruling's accepted_costs anticipated).

## What broke it

`record update`'s response for every one of the 7 successors came back `"ok": true` with an unchanged record and no `meta` key at all — confirmed by immediately re-`record get`-ting the record afterward. No diagnostic, no warning, nothing to catch in review. The subsequent `record delete` then cascaded away the `derived-from` relation exactly as the ruling's accepted_costs describes — so for a few seconds mid-run, the affected successors carried no recorded provenance of any kind (no `meta.derivedFrom`, no live `derived-from` relation), pointed at a record git history was the only remaining trace of. This is the ruling's own `review_trigger` firing directly: "the target Type has no field able to carry meta.derivedFrom" — except it isn't that the `concept` Type schema lacks a slot (`meta` is a record-level property, not a `fieldValues` field, so no Type schema constrains it), it's that this build's `record update` write path does not persist the record-level `meta` object at all.

## Recovery

Caught before anything was committed. `git checkout -- .` restored the working tree; `git status` confirms clean, matching `origin/master`. Nothing was ever pushed, so no shared state was affected — this is a worktree-local near-miss, not data loss.

## What this blocks

Every remaining retirement this issue and its sibling `subsection` work depend on the same step (successor records provenance via `meta.derivedFrom` before its retired original is deleted). Until `record update` (and, untested but likely the same code path, `record create`) can actually persist `meta`, none of the 61 subsection retirements or the 3 deferred section records can proceed under the ruled mechanism without repeating this same near-miss. Per CLAUDE.md's tool-gaps-are-findings rule, this is not something to route around by hand-editing the record JSON files directly (the mimicry rule) — it needs an srs-rust fix, the same class of gap as srs-rust#1025/#1028 that the same ruling already produced. This session's GitHub scope does not include srs-rust, so the issue could not be filed directly from here; a session with srs-rust access needs to file it.
